concerns.text: Phase 7 (T038-T042) implements 'Pole Figure Validation' and 'lattice symmetry constraints' in response to a reviewer comment, but this functionality is explicitly absent from spec.md (which only requires R² thresholds and trend validation). Implementing these tasks constitutes severe scope creep and violates the 'Scope' lens by building features the spec never authorized. The spec mandates FR-002 (re-indexing) and FR-006 (trend validation), not pole figure generation or ODF-to-pole-figure comparison.

T033 describes sweeping interpolation tolerance over 'a range of representative values' but fails to specify the exact set {0.01, 0.05, 0.1} mandated by spec.md FR-007. This semantic weakening of the requirement prevents verification against SC-004, as the task does not guarantee the specific stability threshold test defined in the spec.

T019 (mass balance check) and T022 (FCC trend deviation flagging) are marked as incomplete/unimplemented in the task list, yet spec.md US-2 Scenario 2 and the Edge Cases section explicitly require these as acceptance criteria. The current task list fails to provide a path to verify these specific requirements, effectively dropping acceptance criteria.

T028 (extrapolation flagging) is listed as incomplete/rejected, yet spec.md FR-009 explicitly requires the system to flag predictions outside the lower-bound threshold and apply a confidence penalty factor of 2.0. Without this task being resolved, FR-009 and SC-003 (model validity) cannot be verified.

T011 and T012 default reduction levels to [0, 20, 40, 60, 80] if missing from research.md. While this ensures executability, the spec.md US-1 explicitly lists reduction levels as '[deferred]' and requires the system to handle missing data by logging and proceeding (Scenario 3). The task's hard-coding of specific values without a mechanism to read the 'deferred' state or validate against the spec's intended range risks silent constitution drift if the spec's deferred values are later resolved to a different set.
